title: registerMode: top-level mode registry, co-designed with the status-line seam
wave: 5 (M2 wave 5 — registerMode: phần việc thực chất của M2)
one_line: Extension authors get one `pi.registerMode` call that installs a mode (tools, settings gate, enter/exit, write policy, and a visible status-line chip) instead of hand-rolling 15 KB of mode machinery, and the five built-in modes are re-registered through that same path without changing behaviour.
user_visible_effect: Nothing changes for a user who never installs a third-party mode — the five built-in modes render, gate and block writes exactly as they do today. What changes is that a mode installed from outside the repo can no longer be invisible: `ModeDefinition.statusLine` is a required field, so a registered mode always produces a chip in the status line's existing `mode` segment, in the same accent/warning tones and with the same pause suffix the built-in modes already use. The one user-visible removal: `examples/extensions/plan-mode.ts` (549 lines) is deleted and replaced by a ~50-line `registerMode` call, so anyone who copied that example loses its prose and keeps its behaviour.

steps.instruction: DO THIS BEFORE ANY CODE: get the M2-OQ3 status-line seam decision signed off in writing. The decision must satisfy four constraints verified against HEAD: (1) the 27-member union at schema.ts:2-30 stays closed; (2) a registered mode renders inside the existing `mode` segment (segments.ts:364), not as a new id; (3) the five-way priority chain plan→prewalk→goal→vibe→loop (segments.ts:369-403) is preserved and its order comes from the registry, not from the filesystem; (4) `ModeDefinition.statusLine` is REQUIRED, never optional. The plan's own §7.4 option 3 ('mode segment reads id from ModeRegistry') is the only one of the three that meets all four — but the plan explicitly did NOT choose, so a human picks. Everything in steps 3+ is gated on this.

Write `packages/coding-agent/test/plan-mode/write-policy.test.ts` FIRST, before the policy exists. It must prove BOTH halves: a mode whose writePolicy denies working-tree writes REJECTS a `src/foo.ts` write, AND the SAME mode ALLOWS a `local://slug-plan.md` write. One assertion without the other is a test that passes on an implementation which also blocks the sandbox. Drive it through a registry-supplied policy, not through the built-in plan mode — the built-in inequality is already covered at test/tools/plan-mode-guard-local.test.ts:90-127, and restating it here is a banned duplicate.

Extract the policy as data in a NEW commit that touches no mode registry. `enforcePlanModeWrite` reads the active mode's writePolicy, calls the evaluator, and throws the existing `ToolError` strings keyed by violation kind (core owns the text; an extension must not be able to inject user-facing strings into a tool error). Verify the messages still match the regexes the existing tests assert: /working tree is read-only/, /deleting files is not allowed/, /renaming files is not allowed/. Land and prove this commit alone.

Add `ModeRegistry` + the `ModeDefinition` type. Registry owns: id→definition map, a deterministic order (WI-2's output), active/paused state per id, and `resolvedMode()` returning the single winner for the status line. Reject duplicate ids at registration with a thrown Error naming the id. No `any`, no `ReturnType<>`, `#private` fields only, top-level imports only, star re-export from modes/index.ts.

Convert the 7 mode-state fields (lines 908-915) into getter/setter pairs backed by the registry. This must be a SEPARATE commit from step 3. A bare getter is not enough — there are 28 `this.<mode>.x = ` assignment sites in this file alone (planModeEnabled x4, planModePaused x5, vibeModeEnabled x3, goalModeEnabled x7, goalModePaused x7, loopModeEnabled x2, loopModePaused x4), so each pair needs a setter that routes the write into the registry. After this commit run the two grep gates below and confirm zero new diff sites.

Back the four accessors (getPlanModeState :6132, getPrewalkState :6137, getGoalModeState :6155, getVibeModeState :6163) with the registry, preserving name, exact return type, and returning `undefined` when inactive. `getPrewalkState` returns `Prewalk | undefined`, NOT a boolean — a derived boolean getter cannot replace it. Then re-run the seam-2 grep: it must still be exactly 51 lines across 21 files, 0 of them hand-edited.

Implement the M2-OQ3 seam per the step-0 decision. Add ONE new `SegmentContext` field carrying the resolved mode's display contribution, next to the five existing hardcoded mode fields. Thread it through `status-line-host.ts`. In `segments.ts` `modeSegment`, read the new field first and fall through to the existing chain unchanged. Leave `schema.ts` closed. Write `packages/tui/test/status-line-extension-mode.test.ts` in this same commit.

Seed the registry by WRAPPING, never rewriting: register plan mode first, then goal, vibe, loop, prewalk. Each wrapped definition delegates `enter`/`exit` to the existing `InteractiveMode` method; the original code stays where it is. Re-run the seam-1 grep after every single mode migrated.

Write `test/modes/mode-registry.test.ts`. For EACH of the five migrated modes assert observable equivalence against the pre-migration build: identical tool set after `enter`, identical `mode` value reported back to the extension, identical settings-domain resolve. Assert observable session state — never 'the registry was called'.

Add `registerMode(definition: ModeDefinition): void` to `ExtensionAPI`, following the registerTool/registerCommand/registerFlag pattern. Bind it in the extension loader and record the owning source id so unload can drop that extension's modes. Do NOT add a `ui` alias to `ExtensionAPI` — it has no `ui` member today (verified: the only hit in :1231-1557 is a comment at :1351) and adding one would be a 30th public member on a surface §5.2 counts as 29.

Delete `examples/extensions/plan-mode.ts` (549 lines) and land a ~50-line replacement built on `registerMode` in the same commit. This is a PRECONDITION demonstrating the API is usable, NOT the acceptance gate — deleting an in-repo example proves nothing about an outside extension.

Create the outsider fixture (package.json declaring `omp.extensions` + index.ts) registering: a tool, a slash command, a session_start hook, `ctx.ui.setWidget` (NOT `pi.ui.setWidget` — that would not compile), and `pi.registerMode` with a `writePolicy`. Add NO `registerSetting` line. Then write `test/extension-outsider-install.test.ts`: stage it at `<TempDir>/.omp/extensions/outsider-extension/` and call `discoverAndLoadExtensions([], tempProjectDir)` — never by passing a path into `configuredPaths`, which bypasses discovery — and repeat at user scope via `setAgentDir` + `getAgentDir()`. Assert it RUNS, not that it was found: empty `result.errors`, tool in the tool table, command in the registry, hook fires on event, widget in frame, mode in the registry with its status-line segment. Copy the isolation discipline of plugin-extensions-discovery.test.ts: spyOn(os,'homedir') to a temp home, clear XDG_*, setAgentDir in afterEach.

test_contract: Four contracts, each with a named observable failure. (1) WRITE-POLICY INEQUALITY — `packages/coding-agent/test/plan-mode/write-policy.test.ts`: a mode whose policy denies working-tree writes rejects a `src/foo.ts` write AND the same mode accepts a `local://slug-plan.md` write. Consumer regression: a refactor that hoists the sandbox check above the working-tree branch silently closes off the agent's only scratch space while plan mode is on; the user loses the place to draft the plan and nothing in the UI says why. If this regresses, the agent edits a tree the user believes is read-only — the single silent-data-corruption path in M2. (2) REGISTRY EQUIVALENCE — `packages/coding-agent/test/modes/mode-registry.test.ts`: for each of the five wrapped modes, the tool set after `enter`, the `mode` value reported back to the extension, and the settings-domain resolve are identical to the pre-migration build. Consumer regression: a mode migrates onto the registry but quietly enters with a different tool set, so a feature silently disappears from the model. (3) MODE SEGMENT VISIBILITY — `packages/tui/test/status-line-extension-mode.test.ts`: an extension-registered mode renders a chip in the status line. Consumer regression: a mode with no indicator reads as a bug to the user, because a `mode` segment already exists at segments.ts:364 and they will expect a new mode to appear there. This row is the only thing making that default unshippable-silently. (4) OUTSIDER INSTALL — `packages/coding-agent/test/extension-outsider-install.test.ts`: a real extension written outside the repo, loaded through the real install path, registers a mode with a writePolicy and that mode shows up in the mode registry WITH its status-line segment, and the extension runs (empty errors, tool in the tool table, command in the registry, hook fires, widget in frame). Consumer regression: `registerMode` exists but is unreachable by anything that is not in-repo, which is precisely the false green the plan says in-repo example deletion cannot rule out.

effort: L — a multi-PR milestone, not one change. Budget 5-8 PRs across 4-5 weeks: (1) writePolicy extraction, (2) registry core, (3) accessor pairs on the seven fields, (4) the M2-OQ3 seam + its test, (5) wrap plan mode, (6) wrap goal/vibe/loop/prewalk, (7) registerMode on ExtensionAPI + delete the example, (8) the outsider fixture + install test. Step 1 must be written before the registry exists.
risk: Silently regressing the plan-mode write guard — the one thing in M2 that can corrupt user data. The agent edits a working tree the user believes is read-only and no UI reports it. The failure is invisible precisely because the guard throws a ToolError the user never sees. Two mandatory safeties, in this order: (1) land and prove the writePolicy extraction as its OWN commit before migrating a single mode, so there is only one enforcing implementation in the tree to reason about; (2) keep the mode-state fields as registry-backed accessor pairs for the ENTIRE migration — names and types unchanged, plus a seventh field the plan missed — so a partial rollback is always available. The second-highest risk is shipping a mode registry with no status-line answer: a mode with no indicator reads as a bug, because a `mode` segment already exists at segments.ts:364 and users will expect new modes to show up there. That's what step 0 exists to prevent.
open_questions: M2-OQ3 — HOW does an extension-registered mode reach the status line? This BLOCKS step 6 and cannot be decided by the implementer. The plan analysed three options at §7.4 and explicitly did NOT choose. The four constraints any answer must satisfy, all verified against HEAD: the 27-member union at schema.ts:2-30 stays closed; a registered mode renders inside the existing `mode` segment at segments.ts:364, not as a new id; the plan→prewalk→goal→vibe→loop priority chain (segments.ts:369-403) is preserved with its order supplied by the registry; `ModeDefinition.statusLine` is required. The plan leans toward option 3 ('mode segment reads id from ModeRegistry') as the only one meeting all four, but §7.4 notes option 3 does NOT cover a mode wanting a segment outside `mode` — if that is wanted later, all three options must reopen. Decision owner: whoever owns WI-10 / the M2 design review. Needed before step 6, not before step 0.

Should the writePolicy control user-facing error TEXT, or only the flags? This spec puts message text in core (a `WritePolicy` is allow/deny flags; the guard owns the `ToolError` strings) so an extension cannot inject prose into a tool error. The alternative lets each mode word its own refusal, which is friendlier and is what a shipped example would want. Security-flavoured default, product-flavoured alternative — a human picks.

Does `ModeContext` expose a UI affordance at all? This spec makes it narrow (session, settings, setActiveTools, notify) and hands no TUI handle, because a registered mode's self-drawn area is exactly what WI-13 defines and it lands in wave 6. If a mode is expected to render more than a status-line chip at wave 5, the context needs a seam now rather than in wave 6.

Does the fixture's second leg really need to be a separate commit? The plan's reasoning is sound (tsconfig includes test, so one `registerSetting` line reddens check:ts and the && never reaches the tests) and this spec follows it. Confirm with whoever owns WI-8b that the wave-5 and M2-close gates stay two separate commands rather than one tolerant one.

Should the five built-in modes be registered with their existing `order` values sourced from WI-2, or does WI-2 produce a separate artifact this item must read? Step 7 depends on WI-2's output being a concrete, stable order. If WI-2 lands a diagnostic-only ordering with no canonical list, step 7 has no order to assign and the status-line priority becomes a second, competing source of truth.

plan_corrections.claim: The status-line blocker is the closed 27-member `StatusLineSegmentId` union at `schema.ts:2-30` with no seam for contributors.
plan_corrections.correction: The union is exactly as described (verified 27 members). But the harder half of the blocker is one level down: `SegmentContext` (types.ts:75) carries FIVE separate hardcoded per-mode fields — planMode :96, prewalk :100, loopMode :103, goalMode :109, vibeMode :113 — and `modeSegment` resolves them through a hand-written 5-way if-chain in a fixed priority order (segments.ts:369-403). An extension mode has no field there either, and the if-chain silently returns `{ visible: false }` for anything it does not recognise. A design that opens the id union but leaves the five fields hardcoded still ships an invisible mode, so any M2-OQ3 answer must address both halves.
plan_corrections.evidence: `sed -n '96,116p' packages/tui/src/status-line/types.ts` shows the five fields. `sed -n '364,406p' packages/tui/src/status-line/segments.ts` shows the chain and the `return { content: "", visible: false };` fallthrough. Minor: the plan's 'segments.ts:919-947' for the SEGMENTS record actually ends at :945, and `id: "mode"` is at :365 (the const opens at :364).

plan_corrections.correction: There are exactly 4 call sites and they are not uniform: `tools/write.ts:778` (op update), `:814` (archive path, op update), `:842` (sqlite path, op update), `:859` (op create). The archive and sqlite sites pass a working-tree op over a path that is not a plain source file, so each needs individual reasoning about the new `workingTree: allow|deny` rule. Listing them costs nothing and prevents three of the four being assumed equivalent.
plan_corrections.evidence: `git grep -n enforcePlanModeWrite -- packages/` → 4 sites in write.ts, plus the definition at plan-mode-guard.ts:127 and the existing test file.
